fact: 2010-04-15（周四）：Clare 38 岁、Celia 47 岁；视角是 Clare 第一人称。两人在 Heaven on Seven 吃午饭——Garland Building 七楼、由旧食堂改成的 Cajun 餐馆，靠近 Celia 在 Wabash 的办公室；狂欢节已过两月、复活节也过了，灯上仍挂着亮片珠链，桌上辣酱多到几乎放不下餐垫。
quote: Thursday, April 15, 2010 (Clare is 38, Celia is 47) ... Clare: I’m having lunch with Celia Attley at Heaven on Seven, a former cafeteria turned Cajun restaurant on the seventh floor of the Garland Building, near Celia’s office on Wabash.

fact: 这顿饭是庆祝：Celia 刚拿到 LSW，现已在伊利诺伊州获准执业做社工；Clare 自带香槟，侍者开瓶，两人为「芝加哥儿童的下一个 Jane Addams」碰杯。
quote: Celia just received her LSW, and she is now licensed in the State of Illinois to practice as a social worker, so we are here to celebrate. ... “To the next Jane Addams,” I say as we touch glasses.
anchor: The waitress opens the champagne I’ve brought

fact: Celia 自嘲起步太晚，并点出两人共同点：「Though we are both lesbians with back problems, so there’s that.」她穿所谓的「grown-ass woman clothes」（藏青套装、白丝衬衫），但戴着小巧的塑料鹦鹉耳环；两人吃秋葵汤、交换八卦。
quote: “I dunno, I’m getting a pretty late start. Though we are both lesbians with back problems, so there’s that.” ... her earrings are miniature plastic parrots.

fact: Celia 知道的比 Clare 告诉她的多，虽然她只在「上周 Charisse 的生日会」见过 Beck 一次；她直问「Why her? Why not me?」「Why are you in love with that Becky Charles? I’m the one who’s been waiting for you all this time.」Clare 否认，Celia 说「You are. And she’s in love with you.」
quote: Celia seems to know more than I’ve told her about my recent encounters with Beck, even though Celia’s only met Beck once, at Charisse’s birthday party last week. ... “Why are you in love with that Becky Charles? I’m the one who’s been waiting for you all this time.”
anchor: We eat gumbo and trade gossip

fact: Celia 搬出爱的分类（eros、philia、agape、ludus），说 Clare 与 Becky 之间有「别的东西」，逼她承认；Clare 答「Not in English. Maybe in Greek.」，Celia 回「you two, you’ve got it bad」。
quote: “Clare. There’s all kinds of love: eros, philia, agape, ludus, all kinds, and you might think that what you and Becky are up to is the platonic kind, but there’s something else there. Just admit it. You love her.” ... “Not in English. Maybe in Greek.”
anchor: Celia regards me over her half-glasses

fact: Celia 直接表白「Clare? I love you. Why don’t you love me?」，Clare 答「I do love you. But not the way you want to be loved.」；叙述交代 Celia 情路不顺：她爱过 Ingrid，而 Ingrid 爱的是 Henry，后来自杀了；Clare 说自己爱 Henry、似乎没法再爱别人，「my love is wayward and won’t be oughted into being」。
quote: She tries again. “Clare? I love you. Why don’t you love me?” ... Celia loved Ingrid, who loved Henry and then killed herself. ... my love is wayward and won’t be oughted into being.
anchor: “I do love you. But not the way you want to be loved.”

fact: Celia 问「What’s she got that I haven’t got?」，Clare 答「She’s restful.」；Celia 大笑反驳 Henry 可一点都不 restful，Clare 改口「She’s my friend.」
quote: “What’s she got that I haven’t got?” Celia demands. ... “She’s restful.” ... “You don’t really go for restful! Henry sure wasn’t restful. Really, Clare, what?”

fact: Celia 问「Is it because I’m Black?」，Clare 被冒犯，回「Of course not. Beck is Black, too.」Celia 哼道 Beck 是「the whitest possible Black person. She’s off-white. One drop.」Clare 说「Don’t be mean.」
quote: “Is it because I’m Black?” ... “Of course not. Beck is Black, too.” Celia snorts. “She’s the whitest possible Black person. She’s off-white. One drop.”

fact: Clare 声明「I’m straight, so is Beck as far as I know.」，Celia 说「straight girls are easy」、问她难道没想过；两人斗嘴（「You are such a lech.」「I could give you lessons.」）。
quote: “Celia. I’m not . . . I’m straight, so is Beck as far as I know.” ... “That doesn’t prove anything, Clare. Heck, straight girls are easy. Don’t tell me you haven’t thought about it.”

fact: 转折点：Celia 说 Clare 一生像「Manifest Destiny」、真爱早已铺好路，「Maybe this Becky Charles will break your heart a little. It would be good for you.」Clare 声音发紧地回「I seem to remember being heartbroken when Henry died.」，Celia 语气转软说「But Henry would never have left you. I mean, his last words were—」，被 Clare 一句「Enough, Celia.」打断。
quote: “Your whole life has been one big Manifest Destiny, true love all mapped out in front of you. Maybe this Becky Charles will break your heart a little. It would be good for you.” ... “But Henry would never have left you. I mean, his last words were—” “Enough, Celia.”
anchor: Celia gives me a sly smile

fact: Clare 把手滑过桌面，Celia 握住；邻桌一位白人老妇皱眉，Celia 甜甜回敬「Ain’t they got any lesbians where you’re from?」，老妇移开视线；Celia 说自己穿得像共和党人时比穿得像 RuPaul 更能「obnoxious」。
quote: I slide my hand across the table and Celia takes it. An elderly white woman two tables over frowns at us. Celia smiles at her and says sweetly, “Ain’t they got any lesbians where you’re from?”

fact: 甜点：Clare 要 pecan pie、Celia 要 peach pie，配咖啡；Clare 在收银台付账，两人乘电梯下到黄铜大理石大堂，再走进「异常炎热的四月阳光」。
quote: We order pie with our coffee, pecan for me and peach for Celia. I pay up at the register and we take the elevator back down to the cool brass and marble lobby where we pause before stepping out into the abnormally hot April sun.

fact: 收尾：Celia 手搭在 Clare 裸露的手臂上说「If it can’t be me, then Beck seems all right.」「You’re going to be fine, Clare.」拥抱时 Clare 希望自己能给她所要的；两人在人行道上分手，Clare 看着 Celia 以微跛的步态穿过 Wabash 街，「She doesn’t look back.」
quote: “Seriously for a minute, Clare,” Celia says, her hand on my bare arm. “If it can’t be me, then Beck seems all right.” ... I watch Celia marching across Wabash; her halting gait makes it easy to pick out her slight figure in the crowd. She doesn’t look back.
anchor: “You’re going to be fine, Clare.” Celia reaches up to hug me
